Definition: feminine of a compound of G4642 and G2588; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception:--hardness of heart.
BiblicalUsage: Sklerokardia is hardness of heart, and Jesus names it as the reason Moses allowed divorce. For the hardness of your hearts he wrote you this precept, He told the Pharisees, and after the resurrection He upbraided the eleven for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they believed not those who had seen Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hardness of heart is the one condition that makes God's law bend to man's sin. I hold that the risen Lord still rebukes it in me.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
